body.title: fix: return 412 for matching If-None-Match on non-GET/HEAD in handleCacheHeaders
body.body:
`handleCacheHeaders` returned `304 Not Modified` for every method when the cache validators matched. Per RFC 9110:

- §13.1.2: a matching `If-None-Match` on a method other than GET/HEAD must fail the request with `412 Precondition Failed`, not `304`;
- §13.2.1: conditional headers must be ignored for OPTIONS, TRACE and CONNECT;
- §13.1.3: `If-Modified-Since` must be ignored for methods other than GET/HEAD.

The fix keeps the helper's control-flow contract (returns `true` = stop) while selecting the right status: 304 for GET/HEAD, 412 for a matching `If-None-Match` on other methods, and `false` (handler runs normally) for the ignore cases. Added four tests covering POST/PUT → 412, HEAD → 304, POST + If-Modified-Since-only → 200, and OPTIONS → 200.

Fixes #1623.

body.title: fix(cache): honor request methods when evaluating cache headers
body.body:
resolves #1623

Matching `If-None-Match` preconditions stop POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE with `412` rather than `304` ([RFC 9110 §13.1.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110#section-13.1.2)). These methods ignore `If-Modified-Since`; OPTIONS, TRACE, and CONNECT ignore conditional headers ([§13.2.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110#section-13.2.1)). GET, HEAD, and QUERY retain their existing `304` behavior.

The issue includes a runnable reproduction. Regression tests cover both web and Node adapters, including weak tags, wildcards, nonmatches, and validator overrides; helper-level tests also cover TRACE and CONNECT. They fail with only the source changes reverted.

`pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm build`, and the affected suites passed. Local `pnpm test`: 3,219 passed, 51 skipped, one Node body-limit timeout; unchanged main at f0e1780: 3,128 passed, 51 skipped, two body-limit timeouts, including the same test.

* **Bug Fixes**

  * `CONNECT`, `OPTIONS`, and `TRACE` requests ignore both conditional headers and continue processing.

body.title: handleCacheHeaders returns 304 for matching If-None-Match on POST and PUT
body.body:
### Environment

h3 2.0.8, Node.js 24.16.0. Also reproduced on main at f0e17808ac2439b6434bb10609a961067f4d555b.

### Reproduction

Run in an empty directory:

```sh
npm init -y
npm install h3@2.0.8
node --input-type=module <<'EOF'
import { H3Event, handleCacheHeaders } from "h3";

for (const method of ["GET", "HEAD", "QUERY", "POST", "PUT"]) {
  const event = new H3Event(new Request("https://example.com/resource", {
    method,
    headers: { "if-none-match": '"v1"' },
  }));
  const stop = handleCacheHeaders(event, { etag: '"v1"' });
  console.log(method, stop, event.res.status);
}
EOF
```

### Describe the bug

Every request above returns `true` and sets status `304`. For POST and PUT, the expected status is `412 Precondition Failed`.

[RFC 9110 §13.1.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110#section-13.1.2) requires an evaluated, matching `If-None-Match` to stop POST and PUT with `412`. Returning `false` and continuing these writes would also violate that precondition. The helper already tells callers to stop when it returns `true`, so retaining that return value and selecting `412` preserves its control-flow contract. This does not apply to OPTIONS, TRACE, or CONNECT: [§13.2.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110#section-13.2.1) requires ignoring conditional headers for those methods.

Separately, POST with only a matching `If-Modified-Since` should continue normally, as required by [§13.1.3](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110#section-13.1.3), rather than returning `304` or `412`.

A focused fix and regression tests are prepared.

### Additional context

H3 explicitly supports conditional QUERY requests. Its documented `304` behavior should remain unchanged, consistent with [RFC 10008 §2.6 and Appendix A.5](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc10008#section-2.6). GET and HEAD also keep their existing behavior. `serveStatic` and the ocache-backed route rule already gate their cache handling to GET/HEAD.

### Logs

```text
GET true 304
HEAD true 304
QUERY true 304
POST true 304
PUT true 304
```
